A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RM optimisation framework and retain matching theoretical results and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original RM-versus-GD experiments, including system identification, SVM, GLM, reinforcement-learning, and RNN results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain original experiments and add mechanical-system prediction results and a constrained synthetic optimisation experiment.

M1.justification: v2 adds an RM variant using oracle-based Armijo line search in the mechanical-system experiment. The Gaussian oracle, projection, and minibatch averaging are retained: v1's variance-reduced Algorithm 2 is incorporated into v2's Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: v2 retains the existing experimental coverage and adds simulated coupled mass-spring-damper identification and a 100-dimensional strongly quasar-convex objective constrained to an l1-ball. These extend the represented dynamical systems and introduce explicit constrained experimental coverage.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates Armijo line-search GD alongside fixed-step GD in the mechanical-system comparison (Figures 2–3 and Table 2). The comparator sets in the retained experiments remain RM versus GD.

E3.justification: For random LDSI, RM's step size changes from 1e-5 to 1e-6 and smoothing from 1e-4 to 1e-6; GD step sizes also change. New experiments introduce mechanical prediction testing and constrained batch/smoothing configurations. The SVM plot extends from 10,000 to 100,000 iterations, but v2 still states N=10,000, leaving its actual budget unclear.

E4.justification: Figure 13 adds a targeted sensitivity analysis of smoothing and sampled-direction count, examining constrained accuracy and computational cost. The mechanical example adds fixed-versus-Armijo controls and output-reconstruction/error analysis in Figures 2–3 and Table 2. These questions were not examined in v1.

E5.justification: LDSI run-count reporting becomes inconsistent: v1 states five runs, while v2's Figure 1 caption states four and its main text still states five. This establishes a reporting change, but not an actual reduction in runs. Other retained repeated-run and standard-deviation practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds mechanical test MSEs, including 1.56e-5 for RM-Armijo and 7.85e-4 for GD-Armijo in Table 2, and constrained sensitivity results in Figure 13. LDSI and SVM curves are revised under changed or unclear settings, preventing a same-setting improvement claim. Table 1 and the GLM, hard-function, bandit, and RNN results are retained.

T1.justification: Corollaries 4–5 revise batch-size prescriptions, Corollary 4 changes its iteration bound, and the associated proofs are updated. Definition 2 explicitly quantifies the existence of a positive parameter a. The variance-reduced bounds already appeared in v1 Appendix C; their incorporation into Theorems 3–4 is largely consolidation.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the explicit GD-outperformance and explanatory-mechanism claims. The introduction and conclusion narrow the empirical contribution to competitive performance and superiority in some regimes. The central convergence-rate and proximal-quasar-convexity contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly excludes the bandit example from theoretical guarantees because quasar-convexity is unestablished, and explains the hard function's higher function-evaluation cost. It drops v1's larger-step RM-divergence caveat while disclosing excluded divergent GD runs. The landscape-averaging explanation is retained, moved to Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 documents the mechanical model's parameters, state-space matrices, and Euler discretisation, plus the new constrained-test configuration. It removes v1 Appendix F's public Python-code link while retaining the Python and hardware disclosures. This establishes removal of access information, not disappearance of the repository.

R1.justification: v2 adds Armijo (1966), Hermant et al. (2024), and Farzin et al. (2025b), supporting line search, the synthetic objective, and additional ZO context. The central research positioning remains. The publication update for the existing extragradient paper is not a newly cited work.

P1.justification: Substantial prose rewriting accompanies numbered contributions, expanded explanations, integration of appendix variance reduction into the main framework, relocation of the mechanism discussion, and reordered experiments. Author and affiliation information also changes. Editing is imperfect: v2's Section 4 opening has broken sentence order.

P2.justification: v2 adds mechanical loss and prediction plots, a physical-system schematic, a multi-panel constrained sensitivity figure, and an MSE table. It regenerates the LDSI and SVM plots, moves SVM results into the main text, relabels the RNN diagram, and expands numerous captions.

improvement.justification: The new constrained sensitivity study and mechanical comparisons with Armijo GD and test MSE strengthen empirical support beyond v1. Explicit qualifications also clarify theoretical applicability. These gains are tempered by removal of the code link, contradictory LDSI run counts, the SVM budget inconsistency, and editing defects, supporting a limited overall improvement.
